findings: The canonical 2026-11-07 capture says the purpose is to save payment details during a mobile payment and routes to three platform-specific Payment Sheet URLs (new raw 1–15). It does not capture any of those variant bodies. The matched detailed capture was fetched 2026-04-22 despite its filename and identifies its historical URL variants as mobile-ui=payment-element (old raw 1–12, 1056–1060, 1926–1930). The diff’s final removed paragraph and first added URL share physical line 2919; both exact raw endings distinguish them (old raw 2917–2918, new raw 13–15).

The summary’s central API pattern is historical. The April guide separates a server-created PaymentIntent, a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account or Customers v1 Customer, and a temporary, scoped CustomerSession, matching `customer_account` or `customer` to the identity across server examples. It shows the mobile component and initial `setup_future_usage` setting separately from a later off-session confirmation attempt (old raw 115–130, 140–231, 634–724; source lines 13–44, 63–78).

The April server response and mobile client identity fields do not line up in the displayed Accounts v2 iOS and Android examples. This is a separate issue from the historical React Native and optional Android FlowController credential examples (old raw 178–183, 349–369, 428–450, 486–508, 1198–1203, 1387–1396, 1426–1436 and 1513–1521; source lines 19–44 and 47–58).

The existing summary needs baseline corrections unrelated to the navigation change. It omits purpose-specific consent and the redisplay distinction, has no warning that the archived client samples and endpoint disagree for React Native or that Android’s optional FlowController uses a different credential example, and states an unsupported completion-on-selection and success-only delayed outcome (source lines 13–85; old raw 22–33, 549–552, 620–644, 1567–1582, 1846–1867, 2070–2152, 2248–2355, 2381–2413, 2486–2504).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-04-22 guide described saving during an initial PaymentIntent purchase, with a distinct Terminal card-present flow, explicit agreement for the intended use, record retention, and an `allow_redisplay` boundary for future display (old raw 8–33, 634–641).

The 2026-04-22 guide used the `mobile_payment_element` CustomerSession component and initial `setup_future_usage`, with the cards and US bank accounts limit scoped to that setting. It shows customer-configured Accounts v2 with `customer_account` or Customers v1 with `customer`; the dated Accounts v2 text says generally available for Connect and public preview for others, requiring a preview API version for participants (old raw 115–183, 187–231, 642–648).

The 2026-04-22 guide described a new server-side PaymentIntent for a later off-session payment attempt using the same customer identity and saved PaymentMethod ID, with amount, currency, `off_session: true` and `confirm: true`. An unmet authentication exemption can produce an error (old raw 640–724).

The 2026-04-22 guide separates completing client collection, processing, succeeding, and failing. Delayed payments can still be pending when the sheet completes and later succeed or fail. Server events establish payment status (old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1567–1581, 2411–2413, 2486–2498).
conflicts: The 2026-04-22 Accounts v2 iOS and Android server examples return `customer_account` (old raw 178–183 and 1198–1203). The iOS UIKit and SwiftUI samples read `json["customer"]` (old raw 349–369, 428–450 and 486–508), while the ordinary Android Sheet samples pass `networkResult.customer` from a backend adapter whose mapping is unshown (old raw 1387–1396, 1426–1436 and 1513–1521). Source lines 19–44 and 47–58 leave this identity/payload mismatch unexplained. The archive supplies neither the missing transformation nor evidence of current SDK compatibility.

The old React Native endpoint returns `customerSessionClientSecret`, but both identity branches of its client example instead expect `ephemeralKey` and pass `customerEphemeralKeySecret`; its optional custom flow also uses an ephemeral-key example (old raw 2098–2103, 2144–2149, 2248–2355, 2884–2897). Android’s ordinary Sheet uses `createWithCustomerSession`, while its optional FlowController passes `ephemeralKeySecret` (old raw 1368–1396, 1846–1867). Keep the dated sample differences visible and avoid treating the credentials as interchangeable. Source lines 13–58 otherwise imply a uniform setup.

The source lines 80–85 say the Sheet returns `.completed` immediately on selecting a delayed method and describe only eventual success. The old captures of the integration distinguish selection, completing the sheet, and later success or failure; the `processing` row separately describes a pending state and an optional digital-goods decision (old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1868–1924, 2411–2413, 2486–2498). The archived text does not make earlier fulfillment a signal of payment success.

The in-app concept lines 58–67 can conflate a broader saved-method matrix with the narrower historical `setup_future_usage` limit and says automatic consent handles global compliance. The old guide explicitly assigns responsibility for the intended future use to the merchant and requires purpose-specific consent (old raw 22–33, 115–130, 634–638). A reciprocal source route should warn about both distinctions. The saved-method concept’s mobile route at line 154 should be date-scoped and preserve the distinction from its web `payment_element` example at lines 46–67.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-during-payment, the 2026-11-07 snapshot gives the purpose of saving details during an in-app payment and routes to iOS, Android and React Native Payment Sheet variants. New raw lines 5-15 supply only the index. The detailed 2026-04-22 guide describes a server-created PaymentIntent with mobile `setup_future_usage` limited to cards and US bank accounts, a separate scoped CustomerSession, and either a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account or a Customers v1 Customer (old raw lines 109-132 and 140-231). In the archived Accounts v2 examples, the iOS and Android endpoints return `customer_account` (old raw lines 178-183 and 1198-1203). UIKit and SwiftUI parse `json["customer"]`; the ordinary Android examples pass `networkResult.customer` from an unshown backend adapter. The samples leave the identity mapping and current SDK compatibility unverified (old raw lines 349-369, 428-450, 486-508, 1387-1396, 1426-1436 and 1513-1521). This payload discrepancy is separate from the React Native and optional Android FlowController ephemeral-key examples. Before saving or charging, the April guide calls for purpose-specific terms, explicit customer consent and retention of the written agreement. `allow_redisplay` governs customer-facing display for later purchases (old raw lines 22-33 and 634-641). Old raw lines 549-552, 620-632 and 676-681 distinguish Sheet completion from server-observed payment status and describe a later off-session attempt that may encounter authentication failure. source-stripe-inapp-save-during-payment.md retains the core historical flow and needs those identity, consent and delayed-outcome qualifications.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-during-payment, new raw lines 5-15 replace the detailed canonical response with navigation to `mobile-ui=payment-sheet` variants. Old raw lines 8-12, 1056-1060 and 1926-1930 label the historical detailed variants `mobile-ui=payment-element`. This is a capture-scope change, with no demonstrated substantive product or API change. Keep the 2026-04-22 capture as dated authority for merchant consent and written agreement, mobile `setup_future_usage` method limits, Account versus Customer identity, scoped server credentials, preview version for Accounts v2 preview participants, and `allow_redisplay` (old raw lines 22-33, 115-130 and 634-648). Keep the Android FlowController and React Native ephemeral-key examples distinct from the CustomerSession server payload (old raw lines 1846-1867, 2098-2103, 2144-2149 and 2248-2355). Separately, the dated iOS and Android Accounts v2 endpoints return `customer_account` (old raw lines 178-183 and 1198-1203). The UIKit and SwiftUI examples read `json["customer"]` (old raw lines 349-369, 428-450 and 486-508); Android’s ordinary Sheet samples pass `networkResult.customer` from an unshown backend adapter (old raw lines 1387-1396, 1426-1436 and 1513-1521). The archive gives neither the payload mapping nor current SDK compatibility evidence. In source-stripe-inapp-save-during-payment.md and related concept routes, correct completion-on-selection, make delayed success or failure depend on server-observed payment status, qualify the cards/US-bank limit to this save setting, and preserve the merchant’s consent responsibility. A client completion, return URL, saved method, or initial setup cannot establish final payment success, settlement, or future off-session success (old raw lines 549-555, 620-632 and 676-681).
